title: Big Omega Function
content: Defines $\Omega(n)$, the number of prime factors of $n$ counted with multiplicity, using Mathlib's `Nat.factorization` which represents the prime factorization as a finitely-supported function $p \mapsto v_p(n)$. The sum $\Omega(n) = \sum_p v_p(n)$ counts each prime factor according to its exponent. For example, $\Omega(12) = \Omega(2^2 \cdot 3) = 2 + 1 = 3$.
mathContext: $\Omega(n) = \sum_{p \mid n} v_p(n)$ where $v_p(n)$ is the $p$-adic valuation of $n$

title: Almost-Prime Predicate
content: An almost-prime (or $P_2$ number) is a positive integer $n \geq 2$ with $\Omega(n) \leq 2$. This includes all primes ($\Omega(p) = 1$) and all semiprimes $pq$ ($\Omega(pq) = 2$), including prime squares $p^2$. The sequence begins $2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, \ldots$ The first excluded composite is $8 = 2^3$ with $\Omega(8) = 3$.

title: Decidable Almost-Prime Check
content: A computable Boolean check using `Nat.primeFactorsList`, which returns the list of prime factors with multiplicity. Checking `length ≤ 2` is equivalent to $\Omega(n) \leq 2$ but is decidable, enabling `native_decide` in later proofs. This separation of computable check from the mathematical predicate is a standard Lean 4 pattern for bridging Prop and Bool.

title: Every Prime is Almost-Prime
content: Proves that every prime $p$ satisfies $\Omega(p) \leq 2$ by rewriting `Nat.Prime.factorization` to the singleton function $\{p \mapsto 1\}$, then simplifying the sum to 1. This establishes that the almost-prime sequence contains all primes as a subsequence — a key structural fact showing the almost-primes are at least as dense as the primes.

title: Small Case Verification
content: Establishes the almost-prime status of small integers: 1 is excluded ($n \geq 2$ required), 2 and 3 are almost-prime (as primes), 4 is almost-prime ($\Omega(4) = \Omega(2^2) = 2$), and 8 is not ($\Omega(8) = \Omega(2^3) = 3$). The proof for 4 uses `native_decide` to compute the factorization, while 8's exclusion proceeds by contradiction. These cases ground the abstract theory in concrete examples.

title: Almost-Prime Enumeration and Gaps
content: Defines `almostPrimesUpTo N` as the finite set of almost-primes in $\{0, \ldots, N\}$ using the decidable `checkAlmostPrime` filter, and `almostPrimeGap k` as the gap $u_{k+1} - u_k$ between consecutive almost-primes. The gap function is left as `sorry` — defining it requires establishing a bijection between $\mathbb{N}$ and the almost-prime sequence, which needs well-ordering arguments.

title: Semiprimes Are Almost-Primes
content: Proves that products of two primes $pq$ satisfy $pq \geq 4$ (since $p, q \geq 2$) and are almost-primes. The bound $pq \geq 4$ uses `Nat.mul_le_mul` applied to `Nat.Prime.two_le`. The sorry in `semiprime_isAlmostPrime` needs the multiplicativity of $\Omega$: $\Omega(pq) = \Omega(p) + \Omega(q) = 1 + 1 = 2$. This would follow from `Nat.factorization_mul` in Mathlib, which requires coprimality or careful handling of $p = q$.

title: Primes Contained in Almost-Primes
content: Proves that the set of primes up to $N$ is a subset of `almostPrimesUpTo N`. The proof works at the `Finset.filter` level, converting between the mathematical predicate `IsAlmostPrime` and the Boolean `checkAlmostPrime` via `Nat.primeFactorsList_prime`, which shows a prime's factor list is the singleton $[p]$ with length 1. This gives the density bound $\pi_2(N) \geq \pi(N)$.
mathContext: $\{p \leq N : p \text{ prime}\} \subseteq \{n \leq N : \Omega(n) \leq 2\}$, so $\pi_2(N) \geq \pi(N) \sim N/\log N$

title: The Main Conjecture (Open)
content: States the open conjecture: $\limsup_{k \to \infty} g_k / \log k = \infty$, formalized as: for every $C > 0$ and every $K$, there exists $k \geq K$ with $g_k > C \log k$. This is the $\varepsilon$-$N$ formulation of $\limsup = \infty$. The conjecture is surprising because the almost-primes are denser than the primes (by a factor of $\log \log N$), yet their gaps are conjectured to be relatively large compared to $\log k$.
mathContext: $\forall C > 0,\; \forall K,\; \exists k \geq K : g_k > C \log k$

title: Cube Gap Obstruction
content: Shows that multiples of 8 between consecutive cubes cannot be almost-primes, since $\Omega(8k) \geq \Omega(8) = 3 > 2$. This provides a structural source of gaps: in any interval $(n^3, (n+1)^3)$, the multiples of 8 create 'holes' in the almost-prime sequence. While this alone doesn't prove unbounded gaps, it illustrates how the factorization structure forces gaps. The sorry needs the super-additivity $\Omega(ab) \geq \Omega(a)$ for $b > 0$.

title: Hardy-Ramanujan Asymptotic Density
content: Axiomatizes the counting function asymptotic: $\pi_2(N) \sim cN \log \log N / \log N$ for a constant $c > 0$. This is a special case of the Landau-Ramanujan theorem on the density of integers with exactly $k$ prime factors. The formulation uses a $(1-\varepsilon)$ lower bound for all $\varepsilon > 0$ beyond some $X_0$, capturing the asymptotic without requiring an explicit constant. The extra $\log \log N$ factor versus $\pi(N) \sim N/\log N$ reflects the combinatorial contribution of semiprimes.
mathContext: $\pi_2(N) \geq c(1-\varepsilon) \cdot \frac{N \log \log N}{\log N}$ for all $N \geq X_0(\varepsilon)$
